name: shader
description: The OPTIONAL shader runtime of the effects layer (ADR 0022, ADR 0025): two moving grounds written for this library — mesh (soft drifting colour points) and fold (light panes along slow folds, a soft body and a sharp lit rim) — and halo (light travelling round a surface that works or listens). startShaders() — server-safe, reference-counted, returns its stop function — finds every .fx-mesh / .fx-fold / .fx-halo root, mounts one canvas in the part the effect paints and draws it from tokens read where that part sits, through ONE shared WebGL2 context. A shader is admitted only if it paints pixels it owns, takes every input from a token, keeps the component as its floor and keeps the ink on its part legible — a ground by a QUIET ZONE of its exact base around the copy (--ui-fx-ground-quiet, -quiet-x, -quiet-y), so the ink keeps its audited contrast while the light elsewhere is free; check:fx enforces the first two on the sources, the browser test the last two on drawn pixels. Grounds mix in OKLab from two tokens (--ui-fx-ground-base, --ui-fx-ground-light) and end in a static one-step triangular dither, so slow ramps never band; they render at full resolution (a scaled dither smears) and at most 30fps. Their floor is a still two-stop CSS gradient of the same light. The aurora effect was retired 2026-11-22. The canvas draws the part's own rounded shape (iOS Safari drops a CSS clip on an animating canvas), covers the border box, sits under the part's content or directly after a track's fill so a Slider's thumb stays on top, and follows the component's own state transitions through a registered property (--ui-fx-halo-strength). State is published on the root as data-fx-mesh / data-fx-fold / data-fx-halo (live, still, floor, lost, unsupported); reduced motion draws one chosen still frame and the loop sleeps when nothing moves. configureShaders() and sampleShader() exist for stories and contrast tests.
